name: Proxmox_VE_Topology
description: Cluster, node and guest topology for Proxmox VE: cluster to node, node to guest.
technicalNotes:
OPTIONAL, and off by default. Applies only to a Proxmox resource -- one with the API token -- that also carries pve.topology.enabled=true (lowercase). One per cluster is enough, since it reports the whole cluster from wherever it runs; a cluster with the token on every node runs it once per node for the same map. It shares the opt-in property with addERI_Proxmox_VE, which must also run on every node's resource for the nodes to be drawn. The same property turns on Proxmox_VE_GuestStatus's instance ERIs, which is what draws a guest that is not a resource of its own.

Emits two kinds of edge. Cluster to node, type "Cluster" -- only on a cluster: a standalone host has no cluster row in /cluster/status, and gets no cluster vertex and no Cluster edges. Node to guest, type "Compute", which is the edge that matters: it lets a node's alerts explain the alerts of the guests it hosts.

Guests are matched to their own LogicMonitor resources by MAC address, read from the guest config (net0 and friends). This works because LogicMonitor already keys a monitored Linux resource on its MAC addresses, so the two ERIs meet with no name matching -- a Proxmox guest called "KTV" whose resource is called "KTV - PiKaraoke" still connects. It is the same identity VMware_vSphere_VirtualMachine_Topology uses. A guest with no readable MAC falls back to a synthesised key, as the VMware module does.

A vertex is drawn only if it matches something: a resource, or a DataSource instance carrying predef.externalResourceID. The portal does not render a vertex that matches nothing (confirmed 2026-09-23 -- an unmonitored LXC guest's edge was emitted and never drawn), and an instance can be the match (confirmed 2026-10-19). A guest monitored as its own resource matches once LogicMonitor's own discovery has put the guest's MAC in that resource's predef.externalResourceID, over SNMP or WMI. Every other guest -- unmonitored, ping-only, or an appliance such as Home Assistant OS that answers neither -- is drawn through Proxmox_VE_GuestStatus, whose discovery puts the same MAC, or the same fallback key, on the guest's instance when pve.topology.enabled is set.

Nodes cannot be matched that way. Proxmox exposes no hardware UUID and no MAC for a node anywhere in its API, so each node vertex carries two synthesised keys, and the companion PropertySource addERI_Proxmox_VE stamps the identical keys on each node's own resource: proxmoxve--<cluster>--<node>, and proxmoxve--node--<node>--<ip> with the address /cluster/status reports for that node. The second needs no cluster name, so a node resource without the token matches through its own hostname and system.ips with no property set, and one group can hold the nodes of every cluster. A vertex matches a resource carrying either key; a node whose resource carries neither is not drawn.

The cluster vertex, keyed proxmoxve--<cluster>, is drawn only where something carries that key; LogicMonitor's VMware cluster vertex exists on the map alone, but this portal drops a vertex that matches nothing (seen 2026-10-20 on a two-node cluster).

UNVERIFIED: the name-plus-IP node key (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-20-topology-node-ip-keys-design.md, section 6 items 2-3). Until it is checked in a portal, a token-less node is known to be drawn only through pve.topology.cluster.

Cost: one /cluster/status, one /cluster/resources per type, and one config read per guest. That last is O(guests), which DESIGN section 2 rules out for a metric module -- but this runs hourly rather than every five minutes, and the MAC is available nowhere else, since /cluster/resources carries no network detail.

Like addERI_Proxmox_VE and addERI_Proxmox_VE_Guest, this module cannot be compiled or run outside a Collector. LogicMonitor's own topology scripts do all their work through com.logicmonitor.mod.Snippets -- eriPreProcessor for key normalisation, isMac for validation, generateTopology for the output format -- and reimplementing those would mean inventing a format LogicMonitor does not fully document. The build emits it to dist/scripts/collector-only/ for that reason.
